verdicts.evidence: The sentinel only replaces fm on the no-frontmatter branch, and no field key (title:, impact:, phases:, asi:, tags:, impactDescription:, signature:, nonScope:, appliesTo:, governs:, noTerritory:, noAsi:) matches at line start inside 'Stryker was here!'. Measured byte-identical parseRule and ruleBody output over the 64-rule shipped corpus, 9 crafted frontmatter shapes and 14 no-frontmatter contents (including 'Stryker was here!' itself, 'here!: yes' and 'was: 1').

verdicts.evidence: Removing .trim() keeps trailing whitespace in every scalar field, and that changes a decision: 'impact: CRITICAL ' parsed to 'CRITICAL ' so the r.impact === "CRITICAL" || r.impact === "HIGH" test used by verdict.ts to build the gated set flipped from true to false; 'impact: HIGH\t' likewise, and signature/noTerritory came back as 'sig ' and 'reason  '. No layer went red.

verdicts.evidence: Dropping ^ turns the ASI validator into a suffix match. On a mission rule declaring asi: [XASI04, ASI04X, ASI044], rules --json returned asi: ["XASI04"] where the baseline returned [], adding a fabricated OWASP ASI id to the machine surface and to the distinct-ASI set the compliance draft assembles. No layer went red.

verdicts.evidence: listField(fm, "") builds /^:\s*\[(.*)\]/ which never matches, so the tags field vanishes from the machine surface: rules --json went from 64 rules carrying tags to 0, and explain --json lost tags too. The 848 unit tests, smoke, audit-corpus, spelling and check --strict all stayed green — the field disappears silently.
